description: We are DOOMSDAY, an interdisciplinary team passionate about using technology and science to understand our planet. We bring together interests in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, software engineering, geospatial computing, satellite data, Earth science and data visualization. Our goal is to uncover meaningful patterns in Earth's changing systems and turn complex scientific data into actionable insights.
summary:
Earth Pulse is an open-source, map-first tool for investigating how environmental variables change across locations and over time.

Users select a place and explore monthly records, trend rates, statistical significance, anomalies, forecasts and neighbouring regions with opposing trends. The analysis uses robust Theil–Sen slopes and the Mann–Kendall test (p < 0.05 threshold), while the Opposite Trend Detector compares neighbouring grid cells.

NASA POWER provides meteorological and solar time series; NASA GIBS adds time-stamped Earth-observation imagery, and a high-resolution point workflow can use Sentinel-2 scenes.

The app distinguishes measured inputs, synthetic offline demo data, forecasts and AI-generated scenario illustrations.

Earth Pulse aims to make Earth-system data easier for students, educators, journalists and researchers to explore without confusing a trend with proof or a forecast with an observation.
details:
WHAT WE DEVELOPED

Earth Pulse is an interactive Earth-system investigation platform that allows users to explore environmental changes geographically and statistically.

Instead of requiring users to search through multiple scientific datasets and manually construct analyses, Earth Pulse brings location selection, historical time-series analysis, trend detection, forecasting, satellite imagery and explanations into one interface.

HOW IT WORKS

1. LOCATION SELECTION

Users select a location through an interactive map or place search. The backend retrieves the corresponding environmental records and available geographical context.

2. DATA INGESTION

NASA POWER provides monthly meteorological and solar data, while NASA Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS) provides satellite imagery layers.

The high-resolution point workflow also supports Sentinel-2 Level-2A imagery and vegetation analysis through Microsoft Planetary Computer.

3. STATISTICAL TREND DETECTION

Earth Pulse uses Theil-Sen regression to estimate robust trend slopes and the Mann-Kendall test to determine statistical significance.

Trends are reported with their direction, rate of change and significance information. A p-value below 0.05 is used as the conventional significance threshold.

4. OPPOSITE TREND DETECTOR

One of Earth Pulse's main innovations is its Opposite Trend Detector.

It identifies neighbouring regions whose environmental variables are moving in opposite directions. This helps users investigate why nearby geographical areas can experience contrasting environmental changes.

5. ANOMALY DETECTION AND FORECASTING

A rolling robust z-score method identifies unusual departures from historical patterns.

The forecasting system uses a multivariate RidgeRollout model to estimate environmental changes over a five-year horizon, with p10, p50 and p90 prediction bands to communicate uncertainty.

6. AI-POWERED EXPLANATIONS

A locally hosted Qwen2.5 language model through Ollama helps users understand scientific findings in plain English.

A retrieval-augmented explanation layer supplies scientific context. Guardrails prevent the language model from inventing measurements, modifying calculated statistics or presenting uncertain results as facts.

TECHNOLOGY USED

  • Backend: Python, FastAPI, NumPy, SciPy and scikit-learn.
  • Frontend: React, TypeScript and Vite.
  • Data and geospatial services: NASA POWER, NASA GIBS, Sentinel-2, Microsoft Planetary Computer and OpenStreetMap.
  • AI/ML: Ridge regression forecasting, Theil-Sen estimation, Mann-Kendall testing, K-Means clustering, Qwen2.5 through Ollama and Stable Diffusion v1.5.

CREATIVITY AND INNOVATION

Earth Pulse combines statistical trend detection with geographical exploration and natural-language explanations.

Its Opposite Trend Detector makes spatially contrasting environmental changes easier to discover.

Another important design decision is its evidence-first approach: observed data, synthetic demonstrations, forecasts and AI-generated scenario images are explicitly distinguished.

IMPACT

The platform is intended for students, educators, journalists and researchers who need to explore environmental changes without requiring extensive experience in scientific data processing.

It can support environmental education, regional investigations, scientific communication and exploratory research.

LIMITATIONS AND FUTURE DEVELOPMENT

Environmental datasets have different spatial resolutions and historical coverage. The bundled offline global demonstration includes a deterministic synthetic 15-degree grid, while the repository also provides real NASA POWER ingestion and high-resolution point-data workflows.

Not every environmental parameter has a continuous 40-year record. Forecasts are probabilistic estimates, not certain predictions.

Future development includes expanding real satellite-data coverage, improving spatial resolution, validating models across more regions, strengthening multilingual accessibility and completing permanent public deployment.
